topics.topic: Stamford Land wins High Court claim against UOB over 2021 rights issue share allocation
topics.known_state: The High Court, in a ruling by Justice Dedar Singh Gill, found UOB grossly negligent as appointed manager of Stamford Land's December 2021 rights issue (about 703.7 million new shares at 34 cents each) and awarded Stamford Land $1,887,946.31. UOB breached SGX Mainboard Rule 877(10) by allotting 60,043,712 excess shares to restricted shareholders before fully satisfying 91.4 million in applications from non-restricted shareholders; the related SGX investigation was settled in December 2023 with the company's controlling shareholders donating $2 million to the SGX Investor Education Fund. UOB is reviewing the grounds before deciding its next course of action.

topics.topic: MAS EQDP third batch: five asset managers appointed with S$1.45 billion
topics.known_state: MAS appointed Amundi, Franklin Templeton, HSBC Asset Management, M&G Investments and Natixis Investment Managers under the S$6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP), placing S$1.45 billion with them. This third batch brings total EQDP allocation to S$5.4 billion across 14 asset managers; a fourth batch is under review and expected to be completed in 2027. The appointments were announced by Chee Hong Tat at the SuperReturn Asia Conference.

topics.topic: MAS commits S$20 million from FSDF to GEMS market-maker scheme until Dec 31, 2028
topics.known_state: MAS committed S$20 million from the Financial Sector Development Fund to the Grant for Equity Market Singapore (GEMS) scheme, supporting market makers providing liquidity for around 80 eligible small- and mid-cap stocks and newly-listed stocks until Dec 31, 2028.

topics.topic: PTC grants 7% fare adjustment with adult card fares up 12 to 13 cents from Dec 26, 2026
topics.known_state: The Public Transport Council granted a 7% fare adjustment, deferring 7.7 percentage points of the maximum allowable 14.7%, after SBS Transit Rail and SMRT Trains applied for the maximum increase citing a 21% rise in energy prices and thin EBIT margins. From Dec 26, 2026, adult card fares rise by 12 to 13 cents per journey, concession fares for students, seniors and people with disabilities rise by 5 cents, and Workfare Transport Concession Scheme cardholders see no change. The two rail operators must contribute 30% of their expected fare revenue increase, totalling S$23.94 million, to the Public Transport Fund. The government will spend an additional S$15 million on public transport vouchers, raising each voucher to S$80 and the income ceiling to S$2,100 per person, benefiting about four in 10 households, with vouchers valid until Mar 31, 2028.

topics.topic: SGX records 21 new listings raising S$4.1 billion in FY2026
topics.known_state: SGX recorded 21 new listings raising S$4.1 billion in FY2026, up from six listings raising S$25.7 million the prior year, with an IPO pipeline of about 50 companies, per its FY2026 annual report. The Equity Market Implementation Committee, co-chaired by SGX Group CEO Loh Boon Chye and MAS managing director Chia Der Jiun, oversees initiatives including the S$6.5 billion EQDP, the Value Unlock programme and the SGX-Nasdaq Global Listing Board. SGX chairman Koh Boon Hwee said the number of listed companies is an "outdated metric of success" and that privatisations are a rational and healthy part of the capital lifecycle.

topics.topic: SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye's FY2026 remuneration rises 7.1% to S$8.37 million
topics.known_state: SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye's total remuneration rose 7.1% to S$8.37 million for FY2026 (ended Jun 30, 2026), from S$7.82 million in FY2025, with cash bonus up 8.4% to S$3.54 million, long-term incentives of S$3.54 million, and fixed pay largely unchanged at S$1.21 million. President Michael Syn's gross remuneration rose 16.2% to S$3.45 million and SGX RegCo CEO Tan Boon Gin drew S$2.44 million, up 7%. The pay came as SGX posted record FY2026 results, though supplied reports conflict: one reports net profit up 7.8% to S$698.4 million and net revenue up 13.9% to S$1.5 billion, while another reports record revenue of $1.48 billion, up 13.9%, and adjusted net profit of $759.5 million, up 24.6%. The board proposed a one-off additional dividend of S$0,125 (12.5 cents) per share, lifting the FY2026 total dividend to S$0.57 per share, a 52% increase. SGX plans to fully repay its debt in FY2027 while maintaining medium-term guidance for 6% to 8% group revenue growth.

topics.topic: UMS Integration plans RM450 million placement of 52.94 million new shares at RM8.50 each
topics.known_state: UMS Integration, dual-listed on SGX and Bursa, plans to raise RM450 million via placement of 52.94 million new shares at RM8.50 each (around $2.66 each), a 1.11% discount to its Bursa-quoted VWAP of RM8,595 on Sept 28, managed jointly by CGS International Securities Malaysia and AmInvestment Bank. The placement will not be offered in Singapore and would expand the share base by 5.63% if fully taken up. Around three-quarters of proceeds will fund operations growth in Penang, with the remainder for Vietnam and Singapore. UMS, serving the semiconductor and aviation industries, last traded at $2.63, valuing it at $2.34 billion.

topics.topic: Radiant World judicial management and fraud allegations involving Mizuho Bank
topics.known_state: On Sept 24, a Singapore court appointed KPMG restructuring executives to take charge of Radiant World's key operation unit, removing control from founder Pinkesh Nahar at the request of creditor Mizuho Bank. Mizuho sought judicial management after suing Radiant over US$97.3 million in receivables purportedly arising from iron-ore sales to Glencore International AG, citing strong reasons to believe it was the victim of fraud. Radiant has denied wrongdoing amid allegations it provided falsified documents to secure hundreds of millions of dollars in financing, and top traders including Glencore plc moved to cut ties in late July. Since July, Radiant has cut staff beyond its core iron-ore business, including base-metals unit staff, lost almost half its iron-ore traders in China and Singapore, and seen departures from its London and Geneva offices.

topics.topic: AEM Holdings FY2026 revenue guidance raise and 1H2026 results
topics.known_state: AEM Holdings raised FY2026 revenue guidance to S$630–680 million and posted 1H2026 revenue of S$247.2 million, up 29.9% YoY, with net profit up 875.6% to S$30.8 million. The company provides thermal testing for AI chips via its PiXL technology.

UMS Integration, which supplies precision components for front-end chipmaking equipment to key customer Applied Materials, reported 2Q2026 revenue up 29% YoY to S$87.1 million and net profit up 90% to S$19.8 million.
Micro-Mechanics (Holdings), which sells high-precision consumable tools to over 600 global customers, reported FY2026 revenue up 15.8% to S$75.5 million and a total dividend of S$0.06 per share.

topics.topic: GIC acquisition of 16 Marriott-operated Four Points Flex by Sheraton hotels in Japan
topics.known_state: GIC Pte Ltd acquired 16 Marriott International-operated hotels in Japan for about ¥125 billion (US$800 million or $1.02 billion), taking over the mid-price Four Points Flex by Sheraton chain from KKR & Co, which announced the sale on Sept 25 without disclosing the buyer or price. The chain operates in 11 cities, including Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto and Fukuoka.
